prose.caution: With only 3 New Testament occurrences—each rendered differently—the three 'measured senses' rest on single instances apiece, so the divisions reflect very thin evidence.

prose.def: The pay, wages, or provision-money given for work or service, originally a soldier's rations and stipend.
prose.article: ὀψώνιον means the pay or wages owed for service, and it carries a military flavor from its origins—the rations and stipend given to soldiers. Across its 4 New Testament occurrences the Majority Standard Bible renders it around the idea of serving or wages, as when John the Baptist tells soldiers to be content with their wages (Luke 3:14) and when Paul declares that the wages of sin is death (Romans 6:23). A nice historical detail: Moulton-Milligan note this word was "banned by the Atticists" as too colloquial, yet it became very common in everyday Koine papyri and inscriptions, and Polybius even records soldiers receiving two obols a day as their ὀψώνιον.
